records.name: Audrius
records.facts_used: Audrius is derived from Lithuanian audra, “storm”. The exact masculine name is recorded in the Lithuanian name dictionary; it should not be confused with English Audrey or treated as a spelling of that unrelated name. The exact form is documented in the Senn–Salys Lithuanian–German dictionary of 1968, reprinted in Salys’s collected writings in 1983. This is a dated linguistic record of the name and its relationships; it does not identify the first child registered with this spelling.

records.name: Palemonas
records.facts_used: Palemonas has a literary and legendary setting in Lithuania. The Lithuanian chronicles’ Roman-origin story makes a Roman nobleman of this name an ancestor of the dukes. The story is a historical tradition, not evidence that the legendary migration actually happened. The historical Lithuanian calendar for 1964 prints Palemonas (Palemas) on 11 January. It documents the exact name and its short form in a modern calendar. It neither dates a real ancient bearer nor identifies the unrelated botanical word palemonas as the name’s origin.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: The legendary Roman ancestor is explicitly presented as legend, not a verified migrant or a first personal-name bearer. Botanical VLE palemonas is unrelated. Checked location: 1964 calendar PDF 301 / printed 286; VLE Roman-origin theory and Lithuanian chronicle paragraphs. Original PDF pages were visually read where used; catalogue transcriptions remain attributed.

records.name: Osvald
records.facts_used: Gulbrand Alhaug explains Osvald through Old Norse Os-valdr, with elements meaning “god” and “ruler”. Rajandi also relates the Estonian name to older Germanic forms. The element glosses concern the name’s linguistic history, not a bearer’s powers or character. Rajandi’s 1966 dictionary describes Osvald becoming more common in Estonia in the early twentieth century and cites a frequency of seven per thousand for 1921 in that historical discussion. The figure is evidence about the earlier period, not today’s population or a first-use date.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a reviewed history in five languages.
records.uncertainties: 1921 7 per mille belongs to the historical name discussion, not current population; outdated good-leader gloss omitted. Checked location: Rajandi PDF 139 / printed 141; SNL signed opening etymology. Original PDF pages were visually read where used; catalogue transcriptions remain attributed.

records.name: Ove
records.facts_used: Alhaug traces the Scandinavian name Ove to Old Danish Aghi, a short form of compound names beginning Ag-. He reports alternative meanings for that element: “respect” or a weapon’s “edge”. Neither needs to be selected as the sole meaning behind every Ove. Rajandi’s index records the exact Ove with a Swedish label and Pd 62, a Paide record of 1962. The Swedish context in Estonia and the older Danish family history are different kinds of evidence. The entry does not say how every Estonian bearer received the name.
